run.example: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket

run.note: Use run out of quando vier o objeto

run.example: Let's run over the plan before the meeting
run.note: O contexto distingue revisar de atropelar

run.example: Can we run through the presentation once more?
run.note: Não é separável na maioria desses usos

run.pattern: run away / run away from + noun
run.example: The dog ran away when the gate was left open

run.meaning: mostrar uma ideia a alguém para obter opinião
run.example: Can I run an idea by you?
run.note: Padrão muito útil: run something by someone

set.example: They set up a new account for me
We set off early to avoid traffic
set.note: Também: set off an alarm = acionar um alarme

set.example: The report sets out the main recommendations
set.note: Também: set out on a trip

set.example: Try to set aside some money every month
The delay set the project back by two weeks
set.note: Também: It set me back $200 = custou $200

settle.example: It took the children a while to settle down
settle.note: Também pode falar de vida estável/família

settle.meaning: adaptar-se a um novo lugar ou rotina
settle.example: She's settling in well at her new job
settle.note: settle into a routine = adaptar-se a uma rotina

settle.meaning: aceitar menos do que se queria
settle.example: Don't settle for the first option if it doesn't suit you
We finally settled on a date for the meeting

show.example: He showed up twenty minutes late
He loves showing off his new car
show.note: Com objeto, pode ser separável: show it off

show.example: She showed us around the new office

stand.pattern: stand out / stand out from + group
stand.example: Her application stood out from the others
What does this abbreviation stand for?
She stood by her decision despite the criticism
Everyone stood up when the judge entered
stand.note: Com defesa: stand up for someone = defender alguém

stay.example: I stayed up too late last night
We're staying in tonight and watching a movie

stay.pattern: stay out / stay out of + noun
stay.example: The kids stayed out until dark
stay.note: stay out of trouble = evitar problemas

stay.example: Stay away from that broken step

take.example: Take your shoes off before you come in
take.note: Com pronome: take them off; para avião: The plane took off

take.example: She took on more responsibility after the promotion
A new manager took over the team in June
take.note: take over from someone = substituir alguém

take.meaning: começar atividade; ocupar espaço ou tempo
take.example: He took up cycling after moving to the city
take.note: Também: This table takes up too much space

take.meaning: devolver; retirar o que foi dito
take.example: I need to take this shirt back to the store
There was so much information that I couldn't take it all in

take.meaning: retirar, levar para fora ou convidar para sair
take.example: Can you take the trash out before you leave?
take.note: take someone out = levar alguém para comer ou passear

take.meaning: remover; levar consigo; extrair uma ideia principal
take.example: Please take these empty boxes away
take.note: takeaway também pode ser a principal conclusão de algo

talk.meaning: discutir algo para decidir ou entender melhor
talk.example: We need to talk the options over before deciding
She talked me into applying for the job
talk.note: Padrão fixo: talk someone into doing something

talk.meaning: convencer alguém a não fazer algo
talk.example: He talked me out of buying a new phone
talk.note: É o contraste direto de talk someone into

talk.meaning: explicar ou discutir passo a passo
talk.example: She talked me through the setup process
talk.note: Muito útil em instruções e suporte

think.example: Take a day to think the offer over

think.meaning: analisar todas as etapas ou consequências
think.example: We need to think the plan through before we commit

think.meaning: lembrar, imaginar ou ter opinião sobre
think.example: Can you think of a better solution?

throw.meaning: jogar fora; expulsar; rejeitar uma ideia
throw.example: We threw out a lot of old paperwork
He felt sick and threw up after dinner
They threw in free delivery with the purchase

turn.example: Turn the lights on when it gets dark
Please turn the TV off before you leave
turn.note: Com pronome: turn it off; turn someone off = causar rejeição

turn.example: Can you turn the volume up a little?
turn.note: Também: He turned up late = ele apareceu tarde

turn.example: She turned the job offer down
The event turned out better than we expected
turn.note: Também pode significar apagar uma luz em alguns usos

turn.example: The conversation turned into an argument
Turn the paper over and read the other side
The new manager turned the business around

work.example: We finally worked out what was causing the problem
work.note: Também: work out at the gym; com pronome: work it out

work.meaning: trabalhar em algo ou tentar melhorar
work.example: I'm working on the report this afternoon

work.meaning: resolver ou processar passo a passo
work.example: Let's work through the issues one at a time
We found a way to work around the software limitation

write.example: Write the address down so you don't forget it

write.meaning: redigir formalmente ou transformar notas em texto
write.example: She wrote up the meeting notes that afternoon
The company wrote off the damaged equipment
write.note: Também: don't write him off = não o descarte
